title: Open-source multi-agent LLM framework that produces an auditable trade *thesis* (with full reasoning traces) instead of a black-box signal
author: CampNouMiracle2022
selftext:
Hi Guys! 



Sharing a project I built (open-source, Apache-2.0) because the transparency angle

might interest people here — and I'd genuinely like the critique.



My gripe with most LLM trading tools: they emit a buy/sell with no traceable reasoning,

so you can't audit \*why\* or where it went wrong. \*\*VerumTrade\*\* is my attempt at the

opposite — the whole point is that the reasoning is visible and inspectable.



The pipeline:

\- Specialist analysts gather market, news, social, fundamental, and catalyst evidence

\- Findings are distilled into a structured \*\*evidence graph\*\*

\- A \*\*bull/bear debate\*\* tests the thesis both ways

\- A trader proposes a plan; a \*\*risk review\*\* checks sizing, timing, concentration,

  and crowding/macro-pullback fragility before anything is finalized

\- You get a full \*\*decision trace\*\* — raw evidence → thesis → (optional) order



Data layer is multi-vendor with fallback (starts free on Yahoo Finance); optional

paper/live execution via Alpaca with position-size + concentration guardrails.



Important: this is \*\*decision-support, not an autonomous trader and not financial

advice\*\*. I use it as a structured second opinion, paper-trade first, and make the

call myself. LLMs can be confidently wrong.



Repo + an example report you can read end-to-end:

[https://github.com/muye1202/VerumTrade](https://github.com/muye1202/VerumTrade)



What I'd actually like feedback on: \*\*What do you think is the core mechanism that would level-up this hedge-fund-like debate process materially?\*\* I know that higher-quality data would definitely help, but I'm also interested in how we can upgrade from the aspect of agent architecture.

conclusion rather than genuinely challenge it, and I'd love ideas on guarding against

that
